title: Color output not working in nix derivation
body:
Howdy, I'm trying to figure out how to get color to print from a rust test binary in a nix derivation. I'm using the [dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune) build system to invoke rustc to create a test binary so that I can run tests for my command line app in ocaml. It works great except that in the sandbox it decides to not print color. I noticed that if I hard code ansi colors into panics, it does print that in color but as for the color output of the test info emitted by the rust program, it doesn't even if using `--color=always` and `--no-capture`.

I'm using this expression in ocaml:
```ocaml
let color_mode =
  Option.value
    ~default:"auto"
    (Option.map
       (fun force -> if force = "1" then "always" else "never")
       (Sys.getenv_opt "CLICOLOR_FORCE"))
;;

let cmd = Printf.sprintf "faketty sh -c ./test_ns --color=%s --no-capture" color_mode in
exit (Sys.command cmd)
```

And then I include `CLICOLOR_FORCE = 1;` in my derivation, and after inspecting the environment variables there, it does indeed show it is being set. Locally running the same command without nix does include color, and setting `--option sandbox false` when building the nix derivation emits color as well, although it includes this extra character at the end of where colors are: `(B`. I've tried a bunch of things here to get it working, but I'm stuck. The repo is open source: https://github.com/eureka-cpu/ns

title: Alternatives comparison
body:
I'm curious how this tool compares with the two alternatives I'm aware of. I think it might also make sense to mention them in the README, since you mention `script`.

One alternative is https://www.mankier.com/1/pipetty from the colorized-logs package, https://github.com/kilobyte/colorized-logs.

Another is the `unbuffer` command, https://www.mankier.com/1/unbuffer, which is usually packaged with Done Libes' expect, https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/expect.1.html (it's one of the examples there). I think the official sources for it are at https://sourceforge.net/projects/expect/files/Expect/5.45.4/

title: Turn into library + binary with minimal changes
body:
`faketty` is a powerful binary for capturing colored outputs when testing CLI apps, so it would be great if it can be used as a dev dependency. However, before the eventual stabilization of [`artifact-dependencies`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/cargo/reference/unstable.html#artifact-dependencies), there is no way to pull it into the `[dev-dependencies]` in stable cargo, unless it is made into a library.

> The only other working alternative that I can find is [`portable_pty`](https://docs.rs/portable-pty/latest/portable_pty). It is more versatile than `faketty` but at the same time, much much heavier. So it's still valuable to have a `faketty` lib as a lean version.

Although the diff may seem large, this patch is mostly trivial: it simply splits out a `lib.rs` from `main.rs` such that `faketty` can be reused in cargo projects with `cargo add`:
- Rename `try_main` to `run_command` which takes `Vec<CString>` arguments. This is the only function exposed by the library, along with its possible results (`Exec` and `Error`).
- Make `clap` into an optional (but default) dependency. The library can then be reused without `clap`.
- Document the library use (in README and with doc-comments) and provide a minimal example under ./examples.

title: Reading from /dev/tty
body:
(This might be expected/as designed)

If the program run inside the PTY tries to open and read from the controlling terminal via `/dev/tty` things don't work quite right, but worse they don't fail as expected either.

## Context

This is easiest to see with `sudo` which tries to open `/dev/tty` in order to write the prompt (`"Password: "`) as well as reading the response from the user directly from the controlling terminal. If opening `/dev/tty` with `O_RDWR` fails it falls back to using stdin/stderr which work ask expected with `faketty`. All this can be seen in `tgetpass.c` of `sudo` if interested.

However with `faketty` opening `/dev/tty` works just fine, and even writing to it works as expected, but reading from it does not appear to work.

Example, the password is echo'ed and sending a newline does nothing:

```
$ faketty sudo whoami
Password: foobarbaz

^C
$
```

However, forcing `sudo` to use stderr/stdin works as expected

```
$ faketty sudo -S whoami
Password:
root
$
```

## Question

Is not being able to read from the controlling terminal expected, or is there anything that could be done in this case to set up the controlling terminal to allow reading?

title: Switch Result type to one that can hold io::Error
Exposing a faketty library for use with CommandExt::pre_exec
body:
Thanks for making this ❤️. Have you considered exposing this functionality as a library? When paired with [`CommandExt::pre_exec`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/unix/process/trait.CommandExt.html#tymethod.pre_exec), this would provide the awesome functionality to run commands in a pseudo terminal for other projects. For example by exposing a simple higher order function, this could even allow specifying a custom fake-terminal size or passing through the actual terminal's Termios:

```rust
fn init_faketty(winsize: Option<Winsize>, termios: Option<Termios>) -> FnMut<std::io::Result()> + Send + Sync
```

Would this be in-scope for this project?

Check in Cargo.lock?
body:
<!--  ❤️  -->

It'd be helpful to have a Cargo.lock file checked into the repo.  Primarily, this would let users be confident that they're using the same dependency versions you've tested with, using `cargo install --locked faketty`.  It's also helpful for OS/packager use cases, where you sometimes need to fetch dependencies first, then build offline; I'm currently generating a lockfile and checking it in, as a workaround, but smarter tooling could use a lockfile upstream.

Thanks for the great tool!

title: configurable terminal size
body:
This proxies the current terminal's dimensions (columns, rows) to the child pty or uses the defaults (80, 24).
We also add CLI flags for customizing either or both of these options (width, height).

#### `faketty --help`

```console
faketty 1.0.1

USAGE:
    faketty [OPTIONS] -- <program> <args...>

FLAGS:
    -h, --help       Prints help information
    -V, --version    Prints version information

OPTIONS:
    -H, --height <height>    Sets the height of the pty
    -W, --width <width>      Sets the width of the pty

ARGS:
    <program>...
```

#### `faketty -H this_tall -- ls -shal`

```console
error: Invalid value for '--height <height>': must be a number
```
